description.to:
Build a standalone evaluation system that scores the dataparade-cli scanner's detection across all layers of its pipeline. The system computes precision, recall, and label accuracy as three separate scores (never averaged) and runs without LLM (deterministic mode only).

The scanner currently produces three layers of output:
1. Components — services detected by pattern matching (routes, databases, APIs, auth). These become nodes in the architecture graph.
2. Data flows — connections between components. These become edges.
3. PII signal rules — lexical regex hits for sensitive data (SSN, email, card numbers), currently used only to enrich data flows, gated behind AI flags.

Each layer needs its own evaluation with the same three-score framework but different cases and adapters. The scoring engine is shared; only the adapter (mapping layer output to findings) and the case set differ per layer.

The first PR delivers the shared scoring engine, types, and the Layer 1 (component detection) evaluation with a few fixture cases proving the system works — at least one passing and one failing assertion per score type. Zero scanner changes. Future PRs add Layer 2 (data flows) and Layer 3 (PII signals), the latter requiring a minimal scanner change to extract PII regex matching from the AI-gated path into a deterministic pass.

This issue tracks the evaluation system work. The experimental BDD work (branch DATAP-602-BDD) was the brainstorming phase; this is the production phase — clean PRs against main, no Cucumber, no research-metadata fields in the data, no external repo cloning.
